name: Prospect-Refuge Theory
citation: Appleton, J. (1975). The experience of landscape. Wiley.

constructs.description: Extensive visual access to surroundings. PPA scene encoding → RSC allocentric representation → hippocampal cognitive map → prospective place cells creating richer possibility space.

Protected observation position. Back-to-wall + overhead cover → reduced amygdala threat → decreased BNST sustained anxiety → vmPFC tonic suppression maintained. Mobbs: pre-pre-encounter eliminates both fear and chronic anxiety.

Narrow-to-wide spatial transitions produce spatial PE that resolves as relief, activating mesolimbic reward circuit (VTA → NAc). Sequence produces greater positive affect than static prospect or refuge alone.

schema_gaps: BNST sustained anxiety pathway not directly templated
irreducible_residual.narrative: Compression-release dynamics (Ellard) — the temporal sequencing of narrow → wide transitions and its mesolimbic reward activation — is an organizing principle specific to spatial experience. The predator imminence framing (Mobbs) provides a unique perspective on refuge as 'pre-pre-encounter' safety. Independent T1.5 status beyond Biophilia because it applies to urban design, institutional architecture, and workspace layout independently of natural elements.

provenance.seminal_paper: Appleton, J. (1975). The Experience of Landscape. Wiley.
provenance.predecessor: Gibson's ecological perception; evolutionary landscape preference (Orians)
provenance.historical_context: Appleton proposed that landscape preference reflects evolved survival needs: seeing without being seen. The theory predicts preference for environments offering both open views (prospect) and sheltered spaces (refuge).
